tools.title: Splunk AppDynamics
tools.summary: Application performance monitoring: APM, end-user, infrastructure and database monitoring, SaaS or on-premises.

servers.name: Splunk AppDynamics MCP Server (Docker, stdio)
servers.capabilities: 107 tools and 22 guided prompts over APM, end-user monitoring, analytics events (ADQL), machine and cluster agents and database monitoring.
servers.access: Read operations described (the publisher calls it a read-oriented interface); no enforced read-only mode is recorded.
servers.pin: Docker image tag latest, as documented: each start may pull a newer image.

servers.name: Splunk AppDynamics MCP Server (self-hosted HTTP)

settings.name: mcp_host
settings.description: AppDynamics: the host where your team deployed the MCP server, without https://

servers.capabilities: Same tools as the stdio server, shared by a team deployment that connects to one or several Controllers.
servers.access: Read operations described (the publisher calls it a read-oriented interface); no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

tools.notes: APPD_ENVIRONMENT is the Controller URL and APPD_API_TOKEN a Controller token; the stdio server also accepts OAuth API clients (APPD_AUTH_MODE=oauth with APPD_CLIENT_ID, APPD_CLIENT_SECRET, APPD_CUSTOMER). The docs write --env, registered here as its short form -e. The HTTP server takes the Controller token as a bearer token (--token-env appdynamics=VARIABLE) and an optional X-Events-API-Key header for analytics. Also installable as a Python wheel (3.12+). Documented for SaaS and on-premises.

tools.title: Datadog
tools.summary: Monitoring, APM, logs and security for cloud applications.

servers.name: Datadog MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Query metrics, logs, traces, monitors, incidents and more; toolsets selectable with ?toolsets=.
servers.access: Logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, monitors, incidents, hosts, services, events and notebooks (core toolset; ?toolsets= adds others); write tools create or modify resources, such as monitors, host mutes and dashboards.
servers.scopes: OAuth 2.0 (recommended), a personal or service access token, or DD_API_KEY and DD_APPLICATION_KEY headers; the user role needs mcp_read and, for write tools, mcp_write plus each resource's permission. Org settings MCP Access and MCP Write Access (off hides write tools from every user).

tools.notes: Endpoint differs per site (e.g. https://mcp.datadoghq.eu/v1/mcp, https://mcp.us3.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp); not available on US1-FED/US2-FED (GovCloud). Auth by OAuth, bearer access token, or DD_API_KEY/DD_APPLICATION_KEY headers; Datadog says the server is under significant development and some toolsets are Preview.

tools.title: Dynatrace
tools.summary: AI-powered observability and application security platform.

servers.name: Dynatrace MCP Server (remote)
servers.capabilities: Query Grail data with DQL, problems, vulnerabilities and Davis AI insights from the agent.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

tools.notes: Replace {environment-name} with your environment id. Platform token recommended (needs mcp-gateway:servers:invoke and mcp-gateway:servers:read); OAuth requires a confidential client, no dynamic registration. The local npm server @dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-mcp-server is deprecated (final 2.1.2). GA status read on the Dynatrace Hub page.

tools.title: Elastic
tools.summary: Elasticsearch, Kibana and the Elastic Stack for search, observability and security.

servers.name: Elastic Agent Builder MCP server

settings.name: kibana_host
settings.description: Elastic: your kibana host, without https://

servers.capabilities: Expose Agent Builder tools (search, ES|QL and custom tools over Elasticsearch data) to MCP clients.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: Requires Elastic Stack 9.3+ (preview in 9.2) or a Serverless project; OAuth is GA on Serverless only, API keys otherwise. The docs do not name the transport; streamable-http is assumed. The older elastic/mcp-server-elasticsearch is deprecated.

tools.title: Grafana
tools.summary: Dashboards and observability stack (Prometheus, Loki, Tempo), self-hosted or Grafana Cloud.

servers.name: Grafana MCP server
servers.capabilities: Search and edit dashboards, query Prometheus and Loki datasources, alerting, incidents and on-call; also runs over SSE or streamable HTTP.
servers.scopes: Service account roles and data source permissions. Consent: Provision a Grafana service account token for the intended instance.

read_only.how: The --disable-write flag turns off the write tools.

tools.notes: Works with self-hosted Grafana and Grafana Cloud (set GRAFANA_URL to the instance URL). Also published as the Docker image grafana/mcp-grafana; GRAFANA_API_KEY is deprecated.

tools.title: Honeycomb
tools.summary: Observability for distributed systems based on high-cardinality events and traces.

servers.name: Honeycomb MCP
servers.capabilities: Query datasets, inspect traces, boards, triggers and SLOs; X-MCP-Toolset header limits loaded tools.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

tools.notes: EU endpoint https://mcp.eu1.honeycomb.io/mcp. The team must have Honeycomb Intelligence enabled; only team owners can create API keys, so OAuth is preferred.

tools.title: New Relic

servers.name: New Relic MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Run NRQL queries, inspect entities, alerts, deployments and traces; some AI analysis tools are OAuth-only.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

tools.notes: Paid plan required (not on free accounts); EU endpoint https://mcp.eu.newrelic.com/mcp/, JP https://mcp.jp.newrelic.com/mcp/. API-key auth uses the api-key header with a user key and must be enabled by an admin.

tools.title: Opsgenie
tools.notes: No vendor MCP server found on 2026-11-21: Atlassian's Rovo MCP server documentation lists Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Bitbucket and others but not Opsgenie. REST API only; community servers exist but none was verified as clearly maintained.

tools.title: PagerDuty

servers.name: PagerDuty MCP Server (hosted)
servers.capabilities: Manage incidents, services, schedules, on-call, escalation policies, event orchestrations and status pages.

tools.notes: EU accounts use https://mcp.eu.pagerduty.com/mcp. Requires Advanced Permissions; API-key auth sends `Authorization: Token token=...`. The local server (uvx pagerduty-mcp, repo PagerDuty/pagerduty-mcp-server) is deprecated and archived.

tools.title: Sentry
tools.summary: Application error monitoring, tracing and performance.

servers.name: Sentry MCP
servers.capabilities: Inspect errors, issues, traces, logs and projects. With additional capabilities, triage issues and manage projects. The URL can constrain the organization and project.
servers.access: Search errors, issues, traces and logs, analyse performance, triage issues and manage projects; the URL /mcp/{organizationSlug}/{projectSlug} narrows it to one organization or project.
servers.scopes: OAuth to the user's Sentry account; the page names no scope list. The user reviews the requested capabilities at sign-in, such as inspect, triage or project-management, within their Sentry access.

servers.name: Sentry MCP (stdio via Sentry CLI)
servers.capabilities: Same tools over stdio using the Sentry CLI login; SENTRY_HOST targets a self-hosted Sentry.
servers.scopes: Baseline inspection: org:read, project:read, team:read, event:read; Triage: event:write; Project management: project:write, team:write. Consent: Sign in with the Sentry CLI or provide an authorized Sentry user token.

tools.notes: AI-powered search tools need an LLM provider key configured on the stdio server. The older `npx @sentry/mcp-server` is described as legacy; getsentry/sentry-mcp now redirects to getsentry/toolkit.

tools.title: Splunk
tools.summary: Search, monitoring and security analytics platform for machine data, as Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud Platform.

servers.name: Splunk MCP Server

settings.name: mcp_server_endpoint
settings.description: Splunk: the endpoint shown by the Splunk MCP Server app, without https://

servers.capabilities: Run SPL searches and saved searches, list indexes, sourcetypes, metadata, knowledge objects, KV Store collections and alerts; optional AI Assistant (saia_) and Observability (o11y_) tools.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded. Administrators choose the enabled tools and the allowed SPL commands in the app.
servers.scopes: Users need the mcp_tool_execute capability; creating an encrypted MCP token needs edit_tokens_own and mcp_tool_admin. Consent: each person creates their own encrypted MCP token in the Splunk MCP Server app.

tools.notes: Install the Splunk MCP Server app on the deployment and enable token authentication. The app shows the endpoint (Splunk Web URL on port 443); the older direct endpoint /services/mcp on the management port (default 8089) still works. Send the encrypted MCP token as a bearer token: --token-env splunk=VARIABLE. The publisher's sample config wraps the endpoint in npx mcp-remote. The cloud-hosted *.api.scs.splunk.com endpoint is being phased out.
